Marissa / Rishi — internal notes below to support the customer questions.

Short answers:
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II audited; summary attached. Full report available under NDA.
- Subprocessors: Primary subprocessors for hosted inference are:
  * AWS (EC2, EBS, S3) — model serving and storage in hosted regions
  * GCP (Compute/GCS) — used for some dedicated/private deployments and backups
  * Datadog — telemetry and metrics
  * Cloudflare — edge/CDN and DDoS protection
  * Segment (or equivalent) — product analytics (minimal PII; config-driven)

- Data boundaries:
  * Customer-controlled keys (KMS) available for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted uses Redwood-managed keys but we offer customer KMS integration for enterprise contracts.
  * We do not persist raw PII in training pipelines; logs are scrubbed by default and retention is configurable.
  * Model KV cache and request logs are scoped per customer; we can provide export/delete procedures.

Recommend: attach the up-to-date subprocessor inventory and SOC2 summary to the customer reply, and offer a short call with our security engineer (Aditya) and Rishi (Solutions) to answer data residency / BAA questions.

Attachments (internal): redwood-subprocessors-20260510.pdf

Aditya

Quick answers to your questions:
- Cloud providers: AWS is our primary hosting provider for Redwood-hosted inference. GCP is used in specific dedicated/private deployments and for a small set of backup/analytics workflows. Details are in the attached inventory.
- EU hosting: we have EU regions available for Dedicated and hosted (subject to region availability); we can scope the deployment to EU-only storage and compute where required.
- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood signs BAAs for customers with covered workloads. Typical timeline is 7–10 business days after counterparty review; we can start that process as soon as you confirm you need it.
